title: Software Requirements Specification — Hospital Management System

sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction (Purpose, Scope, Definitions)
sections.body:
### 1.1 Purpose
This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the Hospital Management System (HMS). The system is designed to provide a centralized platform for managing hospital operations, including patient information, medical records, appointments, staff management, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory.

### 1.2 Scope
The HMS will support role-based access for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient. Core functionalities include patient registration, appointment scheduling, OPD/IPD management, electronic medical records (EMR), laboratory test management, pharmacy inventory, bed/ward management, and billing. The system will feature a patient portal and doctor dashboards, along with administrative tools for reports, audit logs, and security management.

### 1.3 Definitions
- **HMS**: Hospital Management System.
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Record.
- **OPD**: Outpatient Department.
- **IPD**: Inpatient Department.
- **PHI**: Protected Health Information.
- **RTO**: Recovery Time Objective.
- **RPO**: Recovery Point Objective.

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body:
### 2.1 System Architecture
The system will utilize a modular architecture with the following technology stack:
- **Frontend**: React/Next.js for a responsive web UI.
- **Backend**: FastAPI, Node.js, or Spring Boot for API services.
- **Database**: PostgreSQL or MySQL for relational data storage.
- **APIs**: RESTful APIs for client-server communication.
- **Authentication**: JWT/OAuth-based authentication.
- **Caching/Queues**: Redis for caching and task queues.
- **Deployment**: Cloud or on-premise deployment options.

### 2.2 System Modules
The system will be divided into the following modules:
1. Authentication
2. Patients
3. Appointments
4. EMR
5. Doctors
6. Nursing
7. Laboratory
8. Pharmacy
9. Billing
10. Inventory
11. Staff
12. Reports
13. Notifications
14. Administration

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: Implement JWT/OAuth-based authentication with role-based access control for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient.
Provide patient registration and profile management capabilities, including personal details, medical history, and allergies.
Enable appointment scheduling and queue management, including doctor availability checks.
Support electronic medical records, including diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, and nursing notes.
Manage laboratory test requests and reports, including result entry and notification to doctors.
Handle pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory management, including stock levels and dispensing.
Process billing and payments, including insurance management, invoices, and receipts.
Manage hospital inventory and procurement, including stock tracking and reorder alerts.
Provide staff management capabilities, including role assignment and performance tracking.
Generate reports for various hospital operations, including patient statistics, financial summaries, and inventory reports.
Send notifications to users for appointments, test results, and other relevant events.
Provide administrative tools for system configuration, user management, and audit log review.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### 4.1 Performance
- The system must support a responsive web UI and fast API responses.
- Scalability must be ensured to handle increasing user loads.

### 4.2 Security
- **PHI Encryption**: All Protected Health Information (PHI) must be encrypted at rest using AES-256, per HIPAA §164.312.
- **Authentication**: Secure authentication mechanisms with password encryption and session management.
- **HTTPS**: All data in transit must be encrypted using HTTPS.
- **Audit Trail**: Immutable audit logs must be maintained for all critical operations, per HIPAA §164.312.

### 4.3 Reliability
- **High Availability**: The system must maintain high availability to ensure continuous access to critical services.
- **RTO/RPO**: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) must be less than 1 hour, and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) must be less than 5 minutes, per healthcare domain benchmarks.

### 4.4 Compliance
- **HIPAA**: The system must comply with HIPAA regulations for the protection of PHI.
- **GDPR**: If EU patients are involved, the system must comply with GDPR data protection requirements.
- **HL7 FHIR**: The system should support HL7 FHIR standards for interoperability with other healthcare systems.
- **DICOM**: The system should support DICOM standards for medical imaging data.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements
sections.body:
### 5.1 APIs
- **REST APIs**: The system will expose RESTful APIs for client-server communication.
- **Authentication**: JWT/OAuth-based authentication for API access.

### 5.2 UI
- **Responsive Web UI**: The frontend will be built using React/Next.js to ensure a responsive and user-friendly interface.
- **Dashboards**: Doctors and administrators will have dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes.

### 5.3 Hardware
- **Cloud/On-Premise Deployment**: The system can be deployed in the cloud or on-premise, depending on the hospital's infrastructure.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
### 6.1 System Constraints
- **Technology Stack**: The system must use the specified technology stack (React/Next.js, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot, PostgreSQL/MySQL, Redis).
- **Data Integrity**: Database integrity must be maintained through constraints and validation rules.
- **Error Handling**: Robust error handling and logging mechanisms must be implemented.

### 6.2 Compliance Verification
- **HIPAA Compliance**: Regular audits and penetration testing will be conducted to ensure HIPAA compliance.
- **GDPR Compliance**: Data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) will be performed if EU patients are involved.
- **HL7 FHIR/DICOM**: Interoperability testing will be conducted to ensure compliance with HL7 FHIR and DICOM standards.

Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
